title: Weak thighs and cola-colored urine
objective: Recognize myopathic needle EMG: early (rapid) recruitment and polyphasic units, with spontaneous fibrillations, positive sharp waves, complex repetitive discharges or 'dive bomber' myotonic discharges in some disorders
secondaryObjectives: Explain what each nerve conduction measure reflects: SNAP amplitude tracks the number of sensory axons, while CMAP amplitude reflects motor axons, muscle and the neuromuscular junction together

why.question: What does the study show, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Normal sensory (SNAP) amplitudes argue against a neuropathy; early recruitment of short, polyphasic units with fibrillations and positive sharp waves is an irritable myopathy; cola urine on a high-intensity statin suggests rhabdomyolysis.
parts.modelAnswer: The sensory amplitudes are normal, so it's not a neuropathy. The units are small, short and recruit early, with fibs and sharps: an irritable myopathy. With cola urine on a new statin, it could be rhabdo.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: No strengthening; call the provider for same-day CK and kidney function and statin review; report the myopathic pattern.
parts.modelAnswer: No exercise. Call his provider for same-day CK and kidney labs and to look at the statin, and report the myopathy.

scoring.modelReasoning: SNAP amplitude reflects sensory axons, while CMAP amplitude reflects motor axons, muscle and the neuromuscular junction together; normal SNAPs argue against a neuropathy. Early recruitment of short, small, polyphasic units with fibrillations and positive sharp waves is a myopathic, irritable pattern. Weakness with cola-colored urine on a statin suggests rhabdomyolysis, which can injure the kidneys: no strengthening, and same-day medical care.
